name: Global Cypher Query Contract
description: Mandatory rules the Cypher agent must apply to EVERY generated query against the Worktual OKG. Retrieve and prepend this card on every request.
business_rules: CASE SENSITIVITY: Neo4j labels, relationship types and property names are case-sensitive. Labels are PascalCase (Conversation, SalesOrder, ContactProfile). Relationship types are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (HAS_ROUTING_ATTEMPT, BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT). Properties are lower_snake_case (created_at, churn_score, total_amount). Never title-case a property, never PascalCase a relationship, never UPPER a label.

NODE KEYS ARE NOT ALWAYS 'id'. Registry: Contact=cdp_id, CustomerScore=cdp_id, ContactPoint=identity_id, Insight=insight_id, Recommendation=recommendation_id, Segment=segment_id, Order=order_id, OrgProfile=organization_id, KnowledgeOrgProfile=organization_id, AssignmentSettings=organization_id, WebchatChannelConfig=channel_config_id, SocialChannelConfig=channel_config_id, Product=id (bigint), PlatformProduct=id (string). Every other label uses id.

ANCHOR BOTH ENDS WITH LABELS. These relationship types are overloaded and reused across unrelated pairs: CONTAINS, HAS_LINE, FOR_PRODUCT, FOR_CONTACT, FOR_OPPORTUNITY, FOR_ACTIVITY, FOR_ACCOUNT, OWNED_BY, CREATED_BY, ASSIGNED_TO, IN_QUEUE, FROM_QUEUE, HANDLED_BY, OFFERED_AGENT, FOLLOWS_HOURS, USES_TEMPLATE, APPROVED_BY. Never write (a)-[:CONTAINS]->(b) without labels on both a and b.

TENANT SCOPE IS THE DATABASE. Each tenant has its own Neo4j database. Do NOT add `WHERE n.organization_id = $organization_id` unless the runtime actually binds $organization_id — an unbound parameter makes Neo4j throw 'Expected parameter(s)' and the agent returns an error instead of an answer.

DATETIME vs DATE. Most timestamps are ZONED DATETIME (UTC) and must be compared with datetime($period_start). But DATE-typed columns must be compared with date($period_start): Invoice.issue_date, Opportunity.expected_close_date, Contact.acquisition_date, Contact.date_of_birth, Holiday.holiday_date, Quote.valid_until. Mixing date and datetime raises a type error.

DURATIONS. Use duration.inSeconds(a, b).seconds for elapsed time. duration.between(a, b).seconds returns ONLY the seconds component (excludes days/months) and silently under-reports any span longer than 24 hours.
ALWAYS BOUND BOTH ENDS OF A PERIOD: `>= datetime($period_start) AND < datetime($period_end)`. A start-only filter makes 'this week' silently mean 'this week and everything after'.
GUARD DIVISION: CASE WHEN total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE toFloat(numerator)/total END. A bare toFloat(x)/0 returns null and the answer reads as 'unknown'.
EXISTENCE CHECKS: use EXISTS { (c)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(:Transfer) } or COUNT {}. Bare pattern expressions outside WHERE are removed in Neo4j 5.

NEVER INVENT A TENANT FAN-OUT EDGE. The following (Tenant)-[...]->(x) relationships are commented out in core.yaml and DO NOT EXIST in the graph: HAS_CONTACT, HAS_CONTACT_PROFILE, HAS_CONVERSATION, HAS_INTERACTION, HAS_DEAL, HAS_DEAL_ACTIVITY, HAS_COMPANY, HAS_COMPANY_SITE, HAS_QUOTE, HAS_PROPOSAL, HAS_INVOICE, HAS_SALES_ORDER, HAS_CONTRACT, HAS_NOTIFICATION, HAS_MISSED_CONTACT, HAS_SHARED_NOTE, HAS_KNOWLEDGE_DOCUMENT, HAS_QUOTE_TEMPLATE, HAS_PROPOSAL_TEMPLATE, HAS_INVOICE_TEMPLATE. Match the label directly instead: MATCH (d:Opportunity) — not MATCH (:Tenant)-[:HAS_DEAL]->(d:Opportunity), which returns zero rows.

(Contact)-[:PARTICIPATED_IN]->(Conversation) DOES NOT EXIST. Conversations, interactions, activities, insights and recommendations hang off a Contact through synthetic collection nodes. See concept_contact_history.
IF NO CARD MATCHES, SAY SO. Do not improvise labels or relationship types that are absent from these cards.

name: Contact History Traversal (collection nodes)
description: A Contact does not connect directly to its Conversations, Interactions, Activities, Insights or Recommendations. Each hangs off a synthetic collection node keyed by the same cdp_id. Every 'show me everything about customer X' query must go through the collection hop.
disambiguation: This is the ONLY correct path from a person to their history. (Contact)-[:PARTICIPATED_IN]->(Conversation), (Contact)-[:HAS_CONVERSATION]->(Conversation) and (Tenant)-[:HAS_CONVERSATION]->() are all non-existent and return zero rows.
business_rules: (Contact)-[:HAS_CONVERSATIONS]->(ConversationHistory)-[:CONTAINS]->(Conversation)
(Contact)-[:HAS_INTERACTIONS]->(InteractionHistory)-[:CONTAINS]->(Interaction)
(Contact)-[:HAS_ACTIVITIES]->(ActivityTimeline)-[:CONTAINS]->(ContactActivity)
(Contact)-[:HAS_INSIGHTS]->(InsightCollection)-[:CONTAINS]->(Insight)
(Contact)-[:HAS_RECOMMENDATIONS]->(RecommendationCollection)-[:CONTAINS]->(Recommendation)
Note the plural relationship names: HAS_CONVERSATIONS / HAS_INTERACTIONS / HAS_ACTIVITIES / HAS_INSIGHTS / HAS_RECOMMENDATIONS. Singular forms do not exist.
All five collection nodes are keyed by cdp_id, the same value as the Contact.
CONTAINS is overloaded — it is also (Order)-[:CONTAINS]->(Product). Always label both ends.

Direct edges that DO exist from other nodes to Contact: (ContactProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(Contact), (Contact)-[:HAS_SCORES]->(CustomerScore), (Contact)-[:HAS_CONTACT_POINT]->(ContactPoint) — direction is Contact→ContactPoint, (Contact)-[:HAS_CHANNEL_IDENTITY]->(ChannelIdentity), (Contact)-[:PLACED]->(Order), (Contact)-[:BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT]->(Segment), (Contact)-[:HAS_ENRICHMENT]->(LeadEnrichmentSnapshot), (Contact)-[:HAS_LEAD_SUMMARY]->(LeadSummary).
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact {cdp_id: $cdp_id})-[:HAS_CONVERSATIONS]->(:ConversationHistory)-[:CONTAINS]->(c:Conversation) RETURN c.id AS conversation_id, c.channel AS channel, c.status AS status, c.created_at AS created_at, c.resolved_at AS resolved_at ORDER BY c.created_at DESC LIMIT 20

What insights do we have on contact X?
Give me the activity timeline for this lead

name: Missed Contacts
description: A contact that was offered to a specific agent and not answered. Materialised as its own MissedContact node with reason, channel, offered_at and missed_at.
disambiguation: Three different things are often called 'missed'. (1) Agent was offered and did not answer -> MissedContact node (THIS card). (2) Routing could not find any agent to offer to -> RoutingAttempt.outcome, see concept_routing_failure. (3) Customer hung up before any agent -> see concept_abandonment_rate. Do not answer a MissedContact question with RoutingAttempt data or the numbers will not reconcile with the Missed Contacts screen in the product.
business_rules: MissedContact is a first-class node (ccass.agent_missed_contacts). Key = id. Do not derive it from RoutingAttempt.
Use missed_at for the event date. offered_at is when the offer went out, acknowledged_at is when the agent cleared it.
Available relationships: (MissedContact)-[:MISSED_BY]->(Agent), -[:ASSIGNED_USER]->(Employee), -[:FROM_CONVERSATION]->(Conversation), -[:FROM_QUEUE]->(Queue), -[:FOR_CONTACT]->(Contact).
There is NO (Tenant)-[:HAS_MISSED_CONTACT]->(MissedContact) edge — match (mc:MissedContact) directly.
Grouping dimensions available directly on the node without a join: channel, reason, customer_name, customer_email, customer_phone.
The Agent-side name is Agent.display_name, not Agent.name.
For 'why did it increase', run the diagnostic_template ONCE — it returns dimension, current, previous, delta in a single pass.
cypher_template: MATCH (mc:MissedContact) WHERE mc.missed_at >= datetime($period_start) AND mc.missed_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(mc) AS missed_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (mc:MissedContact)-[:FROM_QUEUE]->(q:Queue) WITH q.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN mc.missed_at >= datetime($period_start) AND mc.missed_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN mc.missed_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND mc.missed_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5

name: Routing Failure / No Agent Available
description: Attempts by the router to place a conversation with an agent, and their outcomes. Used for capacity and coverage questions, not for agent-level missed contacts.
disambiguation: This is the routing engine's view. For an agent who was offered and did not answer use concept_missed_contacts. For a customer who left the queue use concept_abandonment_rate.
business_rules: (Conversation)-[:HAS_ROUTING_ATTEMPT]->(RoutingAttempt) — direction is Conversation to RoutingAttempt.
(RoutingAttempt)-[:TARGETED_QUEUE]->(Queue) and (RoutingAttempt)-[:OFFERED_AGENT]->(Agent).

OUTCOME VALUES ARE NOT GUARANTEED. Never hard-code an outcome list. Run the discovery query first: MATCH (ra:RoutingAttempt) RETURN DISTINCT ra.outcome AS outcome, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC. Filtering on a value that does not exist returns 0 and reads as 'no problems this week', which is the worst possible wrong answer.
Use ra.created_at for when the attempt was made and ra.completed_at for when it resolved.
attempt_number lets you separate first offers from retries; count DISTINCT conversations, not attempts, when the question is about contacts rather than offers.
cypher_template: MATCH (ra:RoutingAttempt) WHERE ra.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND ra.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN ra.outcome AS outcome, count(ra) AS attempts, count(DISTINCT ra.conversation_id) AS conversations ORDER BY attempts DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (ra:RoutingAttempt)-[:TARGETED_QUEUE]->(q:Queue) WITH q.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN ra.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND ra.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN ra.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND ra.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
discovery_template: MATCH (ra:RoutingAttempt) RETURN DISTINCT ra.outcome AS outcome, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC

name: Abandonment Rate
description: Share of conversations where the customer disconnected before any agent was assigned.
disambiguation: Customer-side. For agent-side non-answer use concept_missed_contacts; for router-side failure use concept_routing_failure.
business_rules: Abandoned = ended_at IS NOT NULL AND assigned_at IS NULL.
end_reason and end_actor carry the reason; end_actor distinguishes customer-initiated from system-initiated. Discover the values before filtering on them rather than assuming codes.
Denominator is all conversations created in the period. Guard against a zero denominator.
Conversation has NO queue_id property in the graph — group by queue only through (Conversation)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(Queue). Group by channel using the scalar c.channel property, which is always populated.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) WITH count(c) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN c.assigned_at IS NULL AND c.ended_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abandoned RETURN abandoned, total, CASE WHEN total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE round(100.0 * abandoned / total, 2) END AS abandonment_pct
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) WITH c.channel AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.assigned_at IS NULL AND c.ended_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN c.created_at < datetime($compare_end) AND c.assigned_at IS NULL AND c.ended_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5

name: SLA Breach Rate
description: Conversations whose service level deadline was missed, recorded as SLAInstance.breached_at.
business_rules: (Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(SLAInstance)-[:BASED_ON]->(SLA). TRACKED_BY_SLA and HAS_SLA_INSTANCE do not exist.
The instance label is SLAInstance (from ccass.conversation_sla_state); the policy label is SLA (from ccass.sla_policies). Both are uppercase SLA — not Sla, not SlaInstance.

Breached when SLAInstance.breached_at IS NOT NULL. Filter breached_at within the period for 'breaches this week'; filter Conversation.created_at within the period for 'breach rate of this week's conversations'. These are different questions — pick deliberately and say which you used.
Conversation also carries denormalised sla_status, first_response_due_at and resolution_due_at. Prefer SLAInstance for breach facts; Conversation.sla_status is a snapshot and can lag.
SLA policy name lives on SLA.name; warning thresholds on SLA.warning_threshold_pct.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(si:SLAInstance) WHERE si.breached_at >= datetime($period_start) AND si.breached_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(si) AS breach_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(si:SLAInstance)-[:BASED_ON]->(s:SLA) WITH s.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN si.breached_at >= datetime($period_start) AND si.breached_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN si.breached_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND si.breached_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5

name: First Contact Resolution (FCR)
description: Conversations resolved without any transfer to another queue or agent.
business_rules: FCR = resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND no (Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(:Transfer).
Use EXISTS { } for the negation. Bare pattern expressions inside CASE are invalid in Neo4j 5.
Report the rate, not just the count — a raw fcr_count with no denominator is meaningless.

A conversation with CONTINUES_FROM set is a follow-up of a previous contact and arguably not FCR. If the question is about true first-time resolution, exclude them: NOT EXISTS { (c)-[:CONTINUES_FROM]->(:Conversation) }.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) WITH count(c) AS resolved, sum(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS { (c)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(:Transfer) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fcr RETURN fcr, resolved, CASE WHEN resolved = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE round(100.0 * fcr / resolved, 2) END AS fcr_pct

name: Average Handle Time (AHT)
description: Average elapsed seconds from agent assignment to resolution.
business_rules: AHT = duration.inSeconds(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds. Do NOT use duration.between(...).seconds — it drops the day component and under-reports any conversation open longer than 24 hours, which is common on email.
Only include rows where both assigned_at and resolved_at are non-null.
Anchor the period on resolved_at (when the handling finished), and bound both ends.
Always return the sample size alongside the average — a 3-conversation average should not be reported as a trend.
Per-agent breakdown goes through (Conversation)-[:HANDLED_BY]->(Agent), returning Agent.display_name.
Email conversations skew AHT heavily. Split by c.channel before comparing periods.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) AND c.assigned_at IS NOT NULL RETURN round(avg(duration.inSeconds(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds)) AS aht_seconds, count(c) AS sample_size
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.assigned_at IS NOT NULL AND c.resolved_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND c.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) WITH c.channel AS dimension, avg(CASE WHEN c.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) THEN duration.inSeconds(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds END) AS current, avg(CASE WHEN c.resolved_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN duration.inSeconds(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds END) AS previous RETURN dimension, round(current) AS current, round(previous) AS previous, round(coalesce(current,0) - coalesce(previous,0)) AS delta ORDER BY abs(coalesce(current,0) - coalesce(previous,0)) DESC LIMIT 5

name: Service Level
description: Share of conversations whose first agent response landed inside the first-response SLA deadline.
disambiguation: Service Level measures responses that were on time. SLA Breach Rate measures the ones that were not. They should sum to 100% over the same population — if they do not, you have filtered on different anchors.
business_rules: Met when c.first_agent_response_at <= si.first_response_due_at.
Use first_agent_response_at, NOT first_response_at — first_response_at includes bot responses and will inflate service level on any channel where bot_active is true.
Guard the denominator.
Conversations with no first_agent_response_at are unanswered so far; decide explicitly whether they count as a miss (they usually should for a closed period) and state the choice.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(si:SLAInstance) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) WITH count(c) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN c.first_agent_response_at IS NOT NULL AND c.first_agent_response_at <= si.first_response_due_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS met RETURN met, total, CASE WHEN total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE round(100.0 * met / total, 2) END AS service_level_pct

name: Queue Wait Time
description: Elapsed seconds from entering the queue to agent assignment.
business_rules: Wait = duration.inSeconds(c.queued_at, c.assigned_at).seconds. Never duration.between(...).seconds.
Conversation has no queue_id property — the queue name is only reachable via (Conversation)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(Queue), returning q.name.

Conversations still waiting (assigned_at IS NULL) are excluded by this metric and will make wait time look better than it is during a backlog. Report the count of still-waiting conversations alongside.
Bound both ends of the period on created_at.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(q:Queue) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) AND c.queued_at IS NOT NULL AND c.assigned_at IS NOT NULL RETURN q.name AS queue, round(avg(duration.inSeconds(c.queued_at, c.assigned_at).seconds)) AS avg_wait_seconds, count(c) AS sample_size ORDER BY avg_wait_seconds DESC LIMIT 10

name: Transfer Rate
description: Conversations transferred to another queue or agent, as a count and as a share of conversations in the period.
business_rules: (Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(Transfer). Destination queue via (Transfer)-[:TRANSFERRED_TO]->(Queue); origin queue via (Transfer)-[:FROM_QUEUE]->(Queue).
Agent-side edges are FROM_AGENT, REQUESTED_AGENT and OFFERED_AGENT — all to Agent.
A conversation can have several Transfer nodes. Count DISTINCT conversations for a rate, count Transfer nodes for transfer volume, and say which you did.
Transfer.state tells you whether the transfer completed. requested_at is the anchor date; completed_at may be null for abandoned transfers.
Transfers are the inverse population of FCR — reconcile the two when both appear in one answer.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(t:Transfer) WHERE t.requested_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.requested_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(DISTINCT c) AS conversations_transferred, count(t) AS transfer_events
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(t:Transfer)-[:TRANSFERRED_TO]->(q:Queue) WITH q.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN t.requested_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.requested_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN t.requested_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND t.requested_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5

name: Conversation Volume
description: Count of conversations in a period, optionally split by channel, queue or status.
business_rules: Default to the scalar c.channel property for channel splits. It is always populated. The (Conversation)-[:THROUGH]->(Channel) edge depends on channel_config_id, which is null for a meaningful share of rows — grouping through it silently drops those conversations and undercounts total volume.

If the question needs the configured channel name rather than the channel kind, use (Conversation)-[:THROUGH]->(ch:Channel) and return ch.name, but state that rows without a channel config are excluded.
Channel node properties are channel_type and name. Conversation.channel is the kind (voice, email, webchat, whatsapp...).
Do not mix Conversation counts with Interaction counts in one total — Interaction is a CDP projection of the same event. See concept_interaction.

name: Interaction (CDP projection)
description: Interaction is the CDP-side projection of a CCaaS Conversation, carrying sentiment, outcome and summary for customer-360 use.
disambiguation: Interaction and Conversation describe the SAME event. Never count both in one metric and never join them into one row set — you will double count. Use Conversation for operational contact-centre metrics (SLA, AHT, queue, routing). Use Interaction for customer-level analytics (sentiment, outcome, engagement history).

(Contact)-[:HAS_INTERACTIONS]->(InteractionHistory)-[:CONTAINS]->(Interaction) is the only path from a person.
Interaction also has (Interaction)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(Queue) and (Interaction)-[:HANDLED_BY]->(Agent) — the same relationship types Conversation uses. Always label the source node or you will match both.
Sentiment, outcome and summary live only on Interaction, not on Conversation.

name: Support Agent
description: The Agent node is the contact-centre identity of a workforce Employee. Conversations attach to it via HANDLED_BY.
business_rules: (Agent)-[:IS_AGENT_FOR]->(Employee) — the Agent is the child; the Employee is the workforce record.
(Agent)-[:HAS_SKILL]->(Skill), (Queue)-[:HAS_MEMBER]->(Agent), (Queue)-[:REQUIRES_SKILL]->(Skill).
(Conversation)-[:HANDLED_BY]->(Agent). Never ASSIGNED_TO for a conversation-to-agent link.
ASSIGNED_TO exists but points to a Employee, from two different sources: (ContactProfile)-[:ASSIGNED_TO]->(Employee) and (ContactActivity)-[:ASSIGNED_TO]->(Employee). Label both ends.
(Conversation)-[:ASSIGNED_USER]->(Employee) also exists in parallel with HANDLED_BY. Use HANDLED_BY for agent productivity; ASSIGNED_USER only when the question is explicitly about the platform user.

search_text: SupportCase Queue Load Workload on SupportQueue: open ticket count, assigned count, sla_status, and membership via HAS_MEMBER StaffRole. team backlog queue open tickets queue workload queue SLA status queue team backlog workload queue load (SupportCase)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(SupportQueue) (SupportQueue)-[:HAS_MEMBER]->(StaffRole) (SupportQueue)-[:MIRRORED_FROM]->(Team) (Tenant)-[:HAS_TICKET_QUEUE]->(SupportQueue)
disambiguation: SupportQueue is ticketing (not CCAAS Queue). May be MIRRORED_FROM Team.
business_rules: Live load: count (SupportCase)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(SupportQueue) with is_terminal = false
Cached: SupportQueue.open_tickets, assigned, sla_status
(SupportQueue)-[:HAS_MEMBER]->(StaffRole)
(SupportQueue)-[:MIRRORED_FROM]->(Team) when synced from MyAccount
cypher_template: MATCH (q:SupportQueue) WHERE q.organization_id = $organization_id OPTIONAL MATCH (t:SupportCase)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(q) OPTIONAL MATCH (t)-[:USES_STATUS]->(ts:CaseStatus) WITH q, sum(CASE WHEN ts.is_terminal = false THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_live RETURN q.queue_name AS queue, open_live, q.open_tickets AS open_cached, q.sla_status AS sla_status ORDER BY open_live DESC

name: SupportCase Agent
description: StaffRole is the ticketing workforce bridge to Employee (IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR). Handles tickets via ASSIGNED_TO (L1) and RESOLVED_BY (L2).
search_text: SupportCase Agent StaffRole is the ticketing workforce bridge to Employee (IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR). (SupportCase)-[:RESOLVED_BY]->(StaffRole) for L2

cypher_template: MATCH (t:SupportCase)-[:ASSIGNED_TO]->(ta:StaffRole)-[:IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR]->(u:Employee) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN u.first_name + ' ' + u.last_name AS agent, count(t) AS assigned_count ORDER BY assigned_count DESC LIMIT 10

description: Person who reported a ticket. Path: SupportCase-[:REPORTED_VIA]->SupportProfile-[:OVERLAY_OF]->Contact. Contact may also have Customer sublabel via contact_type.
search_text: Support Requester Person who reported a ticket. Path: SupportCase-[:REPORTED_VIA]->SupportProfile-[:OVERLAY_OF]->Contact. disambiguation: Do NOT create or MATCH a separate Customer node from ticketing. Use Contact (and optional :Customer sublabel). SupportProfile is spoke ops overlay (like CRM ContactProfile), keyed by contact_profile.id; person key is Contact.cdp_id.
business_rules: (SupportCase)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(SupportProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(Contact)

Customer KPIs (lifetime tickets, avg CSAT) aggregate Tickets under this path

cypher_template: MATCH (t:SupportCase)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(sp:SupportProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(ct:Contact) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND ct.cdp_id = $cdp_id RETURN count(t) AS tkt_total_tickets, avg(CASE WHEN t.csat_score IS NOT NULL THEN toFloat(t.csat_score) END) AS tkt_avg_csat_score
examples: How many tickets does this customer have?

name: Opportunity Win Rate
description: Percentage of closed opportunities won during the selected period.
search_text: Opportunity Win Rate Percentage of closed opportunities won during the selected period. deal win rate win rate close rate opportunity conversion win rate deal win rate close rate sales conversion (Opportunity)-[:WITH_ACCOUNT]->(Account) (Opportunity)-[:OWNED_BY]->(Employee)
business_rules: Closed opportunities have stage IN ["closed_won", "closed_lost"]
Win rate = count(closed_won) / (count(closed_won) + count(closed_lost))
cypher_template: MATCH (o:Opportunity) WHERE o.stage IN ["closed_won", "closed_lost"] AND o.closed_at >= datetime() AND o.closed_at < datetime() WITH count(o) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN o.stage = "closed_won" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS won RETURN total, won, CASE WHEN total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE toFloat(won)/total END AS win_rate
